governanceNotes: Deliberate deferral, not an authored suggestion: the boutonniere-deformity literature documents etiology (central-slip disruption from trauma or rheumatoid synovitis with volar lateral-band migration) rather than downstream sequelae, so an outgoing association edge from this primary currently lacks a target with a defensible condition-specific evidence base.

Directionality check recorded: rheumatoid arthritis -> boutonniere deformity is the documented direction (synovitis -> central-slip elongation -> lateral-band subluxation), which is backwards for this primary; authoring boutonniere-deformity -> rheumatoid-arthritis would invert the clinical literature, and authoring boutonniere-deformity -> post-traumatic-osteoarthritis or generic osteoarthritis found no condition-specific supporting studies in the pre-authoring screen (zero PubMed hits for the PIP degenerative-outcome question).

The StatPearls and Ferlic reviews remain the correct anchors for the upstream direction and are recorded here as screening context only; they are not entered as sourceReferences because no outgoing edge is being authored and entering them would imply an edge that the evidence does not support in this direction.

Deliberate deferral, not an authored suggestion: a boutonniere-to-swan-neck-deformity progression search returned zero PubMed records on 2026-09-22, so a progression claim would be pure biomechanical speculation; boutonniere deformity is itself a proximal-interphalangeal flexion contracture, so an edge to the catalog's contractures identity would restate the diagnostic presentation (the ME-41 phenotype-identity barrier); and the chronic-boutonniere literature is rheumatoid-treatment-outcome class (surgical reconstruction series) rather than natural-history evidence, so no defensible target identity exists.
